hypothesis: With cap < n_experts the qwen36 CUDA expert tier can run in streaming mode (RAM LRU + disk, copy at note) and still beat the CPU path on a box whose RAM cannot hold full residency, because 68-73 % of routed experts are served from VRAM and the rest stay on the shared int4 kernel. COLI_GPUS=0, CUDA_EXPERT_GB=6 and CUDA_DENSE=1 are inert without COLI_CUDA=1; the baseline runs did not set them.
model: Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Kreuzzelg/qwen36-35b-a3b-colibri-i4-gs64 container (int4 gs64 experts, int8 dense), 23.0 GB
command: make qwen36.exe CC=x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc-posix CUDA_DLL=1 ARCH=native (coli_cuda.dll: build_cuda.bat, CUDA 12.9, MSVC 14.44, sm_120); SNAP=<container> TOK=<container>/tokenizer.json N_NEW=64 NOSTREAM=1 COLI_TIMERS=1 COLI_CUDA=<0|1> [COLI_GPUS=0 CUDA_EXPERT_GB=6 CUDA_DENSE=1] ./qwen36.exe 16 4 prompt.txt; tok_s = 1000 / decode TOTAL ms/token from [timers]

hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX, 16 cores / 32 threads (OMP team 16), laptop
hardware.ram: 32 GB, ~9-10 GB available during the runs (desktop apps open)
hardware.storage: KIOXIA KBG60ZNV1T02 NVMe, NTFS, container on the same drive; page cache not dropped between runs
hardware.os: Windows 11 Home 26200, MinGW-w64 gcc (Debian stable, posix threads), NVIDIA driver 616.56, CUDA 12.9, RTX 5060 Laptop GPU 8 GB

quality.method: reference arm (CPU path); greedy tokens deterministic across the three runs

greedy byte-identity against the CPU path with QWEN_EXPERT_ACT=f32 COLI_DENSE_IDOT=0, two prompts, separate runs; under the default int8 activations the tokens differ from the CPU path and between runs (see docs/qwen36-cuda-tier.md, Exactness)
